references.name: Lord D’Abernon
references.desc:
British Ambassador to Berlin; primary
diplomatic source throughout, provided the most
detailed running commentary on the crisis

references.name: Dr. Hjalmar Schacht
Walther Rathenau
references.desc:
Foreign Minister; diagnosed the “delirium
of milliards”; assassinated June 1922

references.name: Hugo Stinnes
references.desc:
Industrialist who built a vast empire on
inflation profits; empire collapsed 1925

references.name: Rudolf Havenstein
references.desc:
Reichsbank President whose devotion to printing
money turned crisis into catastrophe

references.name: Anna Eisenmenger
references.desc:
Viennese diarist whose personal chronicle
provides the book’s most vivid Austrian
testimony

references.name: Erna von Pustau
references.desc:
Hamburg businesswoman’s daughter whose
recollections humanize the German experience

references.name: Joseph Addison
references.desc:
British Embassy Councillor in Berlin; dispatches
to Foreign Office are key primary sources

references.name: Karl Helfferich
references.desc:
Wartime Finance Secretary who established the
borrowing-not-taxation policy that seeded
inflation

references.name: Bresciani-Turroni
references.desc:
Italian economist whose analysis of the
Rentenmark’s psychological success is drawn
on heavily

references.name: John Maynard Keynes
references.desc:
Referenced for his warnings about Versailles
Treaty’s economic consequences

references.name: Judith Listowel
references.desc:
Memoirist whose testimony on Hungarian inflation
and anti-Semitism provides key evidence

references.name: Niall Ferguson
references.desc:
Wrote the foreword to the 2010 edition, placing
the book in context of modern quantitative
easing

references.name: Sir John Wheeler-Bennett
references.desc:
Historian cited on Germany’s moral and
physical exhaustion after the war

references.name: Ernest Hemingway
references.desc:
Visited the German border and filed dispatches
on the surreal economic landscape

references.name: General Wauchope
references.desc:
Authored the prophetic 1927 memorandum warning
that Germany was morally mobilizing for a
future war

references.name: Konrad Adenauer
references.desc:
Future Chancellor; signed emergency currency
notes as Mayor of Cologne during the crisis
